title: Late Breaking Results: Statistical Timing Graph Scheduling Algorithm for GPU Computation
problem: Statistical Static Timing Analysis (SSTA) handles on-chip variations by propagating timing distributions; computational complexity demands huge memory and runtime, limiting scalability to large designs.
motivation: As on-chip variation (OCV) effects dominate at advanced nodes, SSTA becomes essential but computationally prohibitive on traditional CPUs; GPU acceleration offers speedup but memory limitations prevent handling large-scale graphs.
method: Statistical timing graph (STG) scheduling algorithm for GPU execution; memory management strategy optimized for GPU memory constraints; tested on 18.2 GB STG workload.
key_novelty: First GPU-accelerated SSTA with specialized STG scheduling algorithm overcoming GPU memory limitations for large designs.
contributions: Statistical timing graph scheduling algorithm for GPU acceleration
GPU memory management strategy for large STG workloads
Up to 4.9x speedup vs 20-thread CPU baseline on 18.2 GB STG
Enables SSTA on previously intractable design sizes
limitations: Limited to single GPU; multi-GPU scaling and comparison with other acceleration methods not discussed.
primary_theme: GPU-accelerated statistical static timing analysis with memory-efficient scheduling
